title: Exact Angle
summary: At the edge of the refraction zone, Ray corners Kael against the relay-station viewport and demands codes from the architect he thinks he recognizes.

panelPlan.text: Kael stands at scratched ballistic glass with dawn beginning below the ridge. Ray enters and keeps a deliberate three-meter distance.
Ray closes the distance and plants one gloved hand on the glass beside Kael’s head, aligning the other hand with his holstered sidearm.
Kael peels one hand from the glass and lowers it to his thigh, refusing the posture Ray wants.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Four hundred miles, and the trail stops at this glass.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I’m not who you think I am.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You always say that before the angle closes.

title: The Glare Gets Worse
summary: Kael stalls while the rising sun changes the light through the observation deck. Ray keeps adjusting his geometry to preserve a certainty the room no longer supports.

panelPlan.text: Ray sidesteps across the oxidized deck, maintaining distance and tracking Kael’s reflection in the glass.
A hard band of sunrise moves across the floor and reaches Kael’s boots; his reflected face changes as the glare strengthens.
Ray lowers the muzzle a fraction, then corrects it upward as if the problem is his stance rather than the man in front of him.

title: Let Them Hear It
summary: In the generator bay, Samuel uses a loud half-sermon and thrown tools to hide Eva’s work on the atmospheric scrubbers from the guards above.

panelPlan.text: Samuel unspools conductive wire around a coolant pipe while talking loudly enough for the words to carry up the shaft.
Eva strips insulation from a control lead and splices the wire into the scrubber panel.
Footsteps pause on the deck overhead. Samuel kicks a wrench across the grating; the crash covers the snap as Eva closes the circuit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: If they want quiet, they built the wrong machine.

title: Pressure Drop
summary: Eva forces the station’s climate controls into a sudden pressure drop. Jessa keeps the failing machinery from turning the experiment into a real evacuation.

panelPlan.text: The scrubber fans reverse with a deep mechanical thump. Loose dust lifts from the generator-bay floor.
Eva watches the pressure indicator fall while Samuel holds the improvised connection in place with a boot.
Jessa arrives at the service hatch, sees the dropping gauges, and manually opens a bypass before the coolant line begins to hammer.

title: Variable Missing
summary: The artificial pressure change breaks the atmospheric refraction on the observation deck. Ray sees Kael plainly and has to decide what to do without the man he came to confront.

panelPlan.text: The view through the ballistic glass shimmers once as the station pressure drops. Ray’s sight picture slips off Kael’s silhouette.
Ray looks again. The mastermind he expected resolves into a tired drifter with one hand on scratched glass.
The weapon lowers. Kael finally turns around, not to confront Ray, but to walk toward the door.

title: Across the Line
summary: Kael crosses the boundary of the refraction zone while everyone else is still deciding what the loss of the illusion means. Eva follows because the question has changed, not because it has been answered.

panelPlan.text: The observation-deck doors open to hard morning light. Ray and the other armed people remain inside with their weapons down.
Kael walks across the exterior service bridge toward ground beyond the marked refraction boundary. Jessa is already at the rig; Samuel emerges from a lower hatch.
Eva catches up at the boundary marker and looks back once. Kael keeps walking into an ordinary single shadow.
